## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uddhata Sutta* (Ud 4.2, PTS Ud 37) is the second discourse of the fourth chapter (*Meghiya Vagga*) of the *Udāna*. The sutta focuses on the spiritual necessity of protecting both body and mind. While modern secondary literature in the dossier does not provide a dedicated study of this specific discourse, its stock descriptive formula characterizing agitated and undisciplined monks (*uddhatā unnaḷā capalā...*) appears widely in canonical contexts, and Mrs. Rhys Davids cites the Udāna commentary (UdA 238) for its traditional glosses on these behavioral terms [Mrs. Rhys Davids 1929].

- Passage-level parallels: UV 31 Cittavarga; T 212.32 心意品第三十二; T 213.31 法集要頌經護心品第三十一; Uv Kg 31 The Mind
- Mentioned in: Ne 10 Āvaṭṭahāravibhaṅga; Ne 22 Yuttihārasampāta; Ne 35 Samāropanahārasampāta; Ne 20 Desanāhārasampāta
